note: Built from news coverage, union contracts, and city/county websites. Departments are added as they're confirmed; if yours is missing, it may not have been reported yet.

departments.name: Kissimmee Fire Department
departments.detail: First Central Florida department on 24/72. Started April 25, 2026 after hiring 49 firefighters, paid for with a new fire assessment fee.

departments.name: Pasco County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Launched its D-shift (24 on / 72 off) in January 2026.

departments.name: Gainesville Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Moved to 24 on / 72 off on Aug. 19, 2024, cutting the average week to 42 hours. City approved the change in November 2023.

departments.name: Levy County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Adopted 24/72 for firefighters and paramedics in a new three-year contract (September 2025).

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (EMS only)
departments.detail: Paramedics and EMTs moved to 24/72 in August 2025. Firefighters are not yet included (see In talks).

departments.name: Marion County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Contract approved June 2, 2026. County must reach 24/72 by Sept. 30, 2029, hiring nearly 250 people for a new D-shift. Chief hopes to get there sooner.

departments.name: Ocala Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City contract with IAFF Local 2135, approved Aug. 18, 2026, commits to a 42-hour 24/72 schedule by Sept. 30, 2029. Until then crews stay on a half-Kelly Day schedule averaging about 52 hours a week.

departments.name: Polk County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Tentative agreement for a D-shift (24/72) reached July 2026, targeting Oct. 1, 2027. Staffing up with 75 positions added in 2024 and 50 SAFER-funded positions. Final commission vote still pending.

departments.name: St. Johns County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3865 is pushing for 24/72 plus about 125 hires. Talks went to impasse in January 2026 and were still in the state impasse process as of May 2026.

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (firefighters)
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3990 is working to move dual-certified firefighter/paramedics onto the same 24/72 schedule EMS staff already have.

departments.name: Orlando Fire Department
departments.detail: A 42-hour week was a key issue in 2025 bargaining (a fourth platoon would need about 135 more firefighters). The November 2025 contract kept a 48-hour week, so it remains a future goal.

departments.name: Boynton Beach Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City Commission approved a 24/72, 42-hour week with no pay cut in June 2022; the change took effect in 2023 after extra hires were trained.

departments.name: Delray Beach Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Emergency Operations firefighters work a 42-hour week on 24 on / 72 off, starting Oct. 1, 2025, under the union contract.

departments.name: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Union contract (2024–2027) moves 24-hour crews from a 48-hour week with Kelly Days to 24 on / 72 off at 42 hours, effective January 2027. The county may push the start back to April 1, 2027.

departments.name: Greenacres Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Adopting a four-platoon, 42-hour 'Spartan' schedule (24 on/96 off/24 on/48 off) instead of a straight 24/72. Set to begin Oct. 1, 2026; start not yet confirmed.

departments.name: Jacksonville Fire and Rescue
departments.detail: The union is pushing for a 42-hour week, which it says would take a fourth shift of about 450 firefighters. The chief says no immediate change is planned; the current contract runs to 2027.

departments.name: Indian River County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: County leaders are discussing a 42-hour week, estimated at 68 more firefighters and about $11 million, phased in over a few years. No plan adopted yet.

departments.name: Tampa Fire Rescue
departments.detail: The 2025–2028 contract keeps a 48-hour week with Kelly Days but adds flex days in 2027 and 2028 explicitly as a step toward a reduced work week.
